blocks.title: <ico-book></ico-book> WHADDAYA MEAN, TOO FAST?
blocks.intro: Native speakers are not really faster. They blend, shrink and drop the small words so that the important ones land on the beat. Learn what disappears and your ear will stop looking for it. One rule first: recognize all of it; say it only in casual speech; never write it in an email.

vocab.sp: a long seat in a street or park
the part of the street where people walk
a place that sells fuel, and sandwiches at midnight
to understand the main idea, not every word

blocks.note: How it works: this lesson is for your ears. The gold buttons play real-speed clips: compare , listening , gap-fill , order , flashcards and memory. Use headphones if you can.

parts.html: 1 · THE BEAT — content words are loud; grammar words are small

items.en: I want to go to the store.
items.sp: Three beats: WANT, GO, STORE. «I», «to» and «to the» shrink to fit between them.

items.en: Can you give me a hand?
items.sp: Two beats: GIVE, HAND. The rest is almost a whisper.

parts.html: 2 · THE REDUCTIONS — two or three words become one sound

items.sp: I am going to be late.
We should have left earlier. The same happens with coulda and woulda.

parts.html: 3 · LINKING — a final consonant jumps onto the next vowel

items.sp: Sounds like «tur-ni-toff»: three words, one piece.

parts.html: 4 · SOUNDS THAT VANISH OR CHANGE — the dropped T and the quick D

items.en: See you next day. Most people know.
items.sp: The T between two consonants disappears: «nex day», «mos people».

items.en: A lot of water is better.
items.sp: Between vowels, American T becomes a quick D: «a lodda wadder is bedder».

parts.html: 5 · CAN vs CAN'T — listen to the vowel, not the T

items.sp: «can» is weak and short, almost «kn»: I kn DO it. The stress is on DO.
«can't» keeps its full vowel and takes the stress: I CAN'T do it. The T is often silent.

parts.body: If the word is long and loud, it is «can't». If you can hardly hear it, it is «can». When it matters (a date, a price, a yes or no), check: Sorry, was that can or can't?

parts.html: SPANISH TRAP — el ritmo del español juega en contra

items.en: I was at the office for an hour.
items.sp: En español cada sílaba pesa lo mismo. En inglés solo suenan fuertes OFF- y HOUR; lo demás casi desaparece. Si pronuncias todo igual, te entienden; si esperas oírlo todo igual, no entiendes.

items.en: I am going to send the report today.
items.sp: Gonna, wanna y gotta se dicen, no se escriben: en un correo, siempre la forma completa.
El error más caro: oír can donde dijeron can't. Escucha la vocal.

blocks.intro:
Roz hands you a microphone and sends you out into the street: one question for anyone who will stop. «Nobody out there speaks like a textbook,» she says. «You won't catch every word. Get the gist first, then go back for the details.»

WORDS OF THE DAY: to mumble = to speak quietly and unclearly · get the gist · catch every word.

blocks.title: AUDIO 1 · THE STREET
blocks.desc: Five people, one question: «What would you change about this place?» This is natural speed. Every question below depends on one small, reduced word. Listen twice before you open the transcript.
blocks.speakers: <ico-commentdots></ico-commentdots> Roz · Sam · Kit · Robin · Max · Marcos

questions.q: Sam says the city "coulda fixed that ages ago." What does that mean?
options: The city had the chance to fix it, and didn't
The city fixed it a long time ago
The city is going to fix it soon

questions.q: What is it that Robin can NOT sleep through?
Max says "We shoulda built a garage ten years ago." Was it built?
options: Yes, but it is too small
No, and now it will cost three times as much
A job with a team overseas

speaking.prompt: Answer the street question yourself in twenty seconds, at natural speed. Use two reductions.
speaking.starter: What would I change? Honestly, I'd… 'cause… They shoulda… I'm gonna…

transcript.html: Street interviews for Friday's show. One question: what would you change about this place? Here's what people told us.

What would I change? Honestly, the buses. I gotta be at the bakery by five, and the first bus is at five thirty. I've been asking for an early bus for, like, three years. They coulda fixed that ages ago. So now I ride my bike, 'cause I've got no choice.

Oh, I dunno. The sidewalks, I guess. My mom can't walk very far, and there's nowhere to sit down. I'm not kidding, there isn't a single bench between here and the clinic. Just gimme a few benches and I'll stop complaining. Well, kinda.

Lemme think. You know what? I wouldn't change much. People complain a lot, but I've lived in bigger cities, and this one's a lot better than they think. If I hafta pick something, it's the noise at night. I can sleep through traffic, but I can't sleep through the bars on my street.

The parking. D'you know how long it takes to park near my store? Twenty minutes, on a good day. We shoulda built a garage ten years ago, when the land was cheap. Now it's gonna cost three times as much. But hey, nobody asked me.

Whaddaya mean, change? I love this place. Okay, okay, one thing. I wanna see more places open late. I work with a team overseas, so I finish at midnight, and by then all you can get is a gas station sandwich. That's gotta change.

blocks.title: THE REDUCTIONS · tap to flip
blocks.intro: The sound on the front, the written form on the back. Tap the speaker, then say the full form before you flip.

cards.back: going to · «I'm gonna call her.» = I am going to call her.
want to · «Do you wanna eat?» = Do you want to eat?
(have) got to · «I gotta go.» = I have got to go.
have to · «I hafta work.» = I have to work.
kind of · «It's kinda cold.» = It is kind of cold.
let me · «Lemme think.» = Let me think.
give me · «Gimme a minute.» = Give me a minute.
because · «I left 'cause it was late.» = I left because it was late.
what do you / what are you · «Whaddaya think?» = What do you think?
should have, could have, would have · «I shoulda called.» = I should have called.

blocks.title: AUDIO 2 · THE VOICEMAIL
blocks.desc: Kit calls the station back and leaves a fast message: a street, a time and a phone number. Take notes as you listen, the way you would at work.

questions.q: Which street does Kit want to show the reporter?

options: Kit is taking a parent to the doctor
Kit will be at the debate

speaking.prompt: Call Kit back and leave a message: confirm the street, the day and the time, and give your own number twice.
speaking.starter: Hi Kit, this is (name) from The Signal. I'm calling to confirm: (street), (day) at (time). My number is… That's…

transcript.html: Hi, this is Kit, I called in after the debate. Listen, I'm gonna be quick 'cause I'm at work. You asked about benches, and I wanna show your reporter the worst spot. It's on Garden Street, between the clinic and the pharmacy. Not Garden Avenue. Garden Street. I can meet somebody Thursday at four fifteen, but I can't do Friday. I hafta take my mom to the doctor. Lemme give you my number. It's five five five, zero one four two. That's five five five, zero one four two. If I don't pick up, just leave a message and I'll call you right back. Thanks a lot!

blocks.title: <ico-mic></ico-mic> SHADOW IT
blocks.intro: This week's task is spoken. Play the twenty-second clip. First, write it down below in full, written forms (no gonna, no wanna). Then shadow it: play it again and speak along with the voice, half a second behind, copying the rhythm.
checklist: Stress: the content words are loud, the small words almost disappear
Linking: no pause between a final consonant and the next vowel
At least two reductions, said the way the voice says them
Can short and weak; can't long and stressed
Your written version uses only full forms
